$comment: Consensus test vectors for the delegation message. Three implementations must agree on these bytes: contracts/Delegation.sol, src/message.ts, and any third-party wallet that signs one. Each case gives the terms, the exact message string and its EIP-191 digest. Both languages are tested against this file (test/solidity/Vectors.t.sol and test/js/vectors.test.ts). CHANGING A LINE HERE INVALIDATES EVERY SIGNATURE EVER GENERATED: it is not a test fixture, it is the specification.

cases.name: no expiry, mainnet
cases.why: The ordinary prompted credential: a deadline of zero renders as the word never, and stays a line.
cases.message:
IMPORTANT: Only sign this on a site you trust.

This authorizes another address to act in your name onchain, at one contract.
You can withdraw it at any time by revoking it there.

Delegate: 0xd8da6bf26964af9d7eed9e03e53415d37aa96045
Contract: 0x5fbdb2315678afecb367f032d93f642f64180aa3
Chain ID: 1
Expires: never

cases.name: a real deadline, dev chain
cases.why: The auto-signed, allowlisted credential: a unix timestamp in decimal, on the chain id a local node uses.

cases.name: checksummed input, lowercase output
cases.why: Same terms as the first case, spelled EIP-55. Both sides must lowercase, so this must produce byte-identical output to it; a checksumming implementation produces a different message and every signature it makes is rejected onchain.

cases.name: the smallest non-zero deadline
cases.why: One second past the epoch: long expired, and NOT the same as no expiry. The boundary an implementation crosses if it treats a falsy deadline as absent.

cases.name: a far deadline, dev chain
cases.why: A ten-digit timestamp against a five-digit chain id, so a decimal renderer that pads, truncates or thousands-separates either one is caught.
